cards.title: Read the structure
items: Illustrative role organization supplied by the operator; not a staffed reporting chart or live deployment claim.
Each stage pairs design/discovery with engineering/production. The two roles are peers within their function.
Lifecycle: 1 ingestion → 2 storage, cleaning and modeling → 3 BI and reporting → 4 advanced analytics and AI. AI may also use governed Silver directly.

cards.title: Data Architect — design
items: data-platform • data-profiling • data-modeling
data-governance • data-catalog
Define storage responsibilities, identity, relationships, grain, time and trusted lineage.

cards.title: Data Engineer — production
items: data-onboarding • data-quality • sql-writer
MDM Engineering contains refining rules: mapping, quality, matching and survivorship changes.
data-operations • pipeline-orchestration • bookkeeping • change-journal
database-monitoring • production-support • aws-snowflake-operations • access-audit • openmetadata

cards.title: Data Analyst / BI Developer
items: Analyst: auto-ontology-product-query for configured business questions; no general analyst workflow skill.
BI: semantic-views • auto-ontology • aws-snowflake-operations • data-catalog • openmetadata.
No generic dashboard-builder, Power BI administration or Tableau administration skill.

cards.title: Data Scientist / AI–ML Engineer
items: Scientist: data-scientist guides exploration, experimentation and prediction.
AI/ML Engineer: no maintained end-to-end training, model serving, RAG or agent deployment skill.
A semantic query integration does not establish production ML capability.

cards.title: Platform boundaries
items: Captured files = Bronze; MDM = mastered identities; RDM = reference code sets; Silver = source facts.
Gold transformations and dashboards are downstream work, not universal deployed stages.
Skill availability means an operating guide exists; qualification, authorization and activation remain separate.

cards.title: MDM people and process
items: Governance leaders set policies; architects/modelers define domains; stewards resolve exceptions; integration engineers automate approved flows.
Govern → profile and model → configure integration → check and match → steward → validate relationships → publish and verify.
Operational golden records and analytical linked views are consumption patterns; generic source-system write-back is not implied.
